resolved_by: The Sentencing Commission resolved the debate by promulgating Amendment 801, effective November 1, 2016, which revised § 2G2.2(b)(3)(F) to require that the defendant knowingly engaged in distribution.
issue: Before Amendment 801, did the distribution enhancement in U.S.S.G. § 2G2.2(b)(3)(F) require proof that the defendant knew of the distribution (a mens rea element)?

sides.position: Pre-Amendment 801, the distribution enhancement required knowledge (a scienter requirement).
cases: United States v. Robinson, 714 F.3d 466 (7th Cir. 2013)
United States v. Baldwin, 743 F.3d 357 (2d Cir. 2014)
United States v. Layton, 564 F.3d 330 (4th Cir. 2009)

sides.position: Pre-Amendment 801, the distribution enhancement's language unambiguously contained no scienter requirement, so it applied without proof of knowledge.
cases: United States v. Baker, 742 F.3d 618 (5th Cir. 2014)
United States v. Ray, 704 F.3d 1307 (10th Cir. 2013)
United States v. Creel, 783 F.3d 1357 (11th Cir. 2015)

quote: The United States Sentencing Commission resolved this debate by promulgating Amendment 801, effective on November 1, 2016.
cite: United States v. Maximus Prophet, 989 F.3d 231 (3rd Cir. 2021)
